themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints spiked to 4 reports this week versus a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—an 700% increase (z-score: 7.0)—signaling either a sudden neighborhood dog control problem or enforcement gap in Tottenville/Great Kills.
evidence: 4 unleashed dog complaints this week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 7.0)
Spike is statistically significant and sudden—no gradual trend, suggesting acute incident or pattern change
Tottenville/Great Kills has higher-than-average residential space and fewer off-leash dog parks, increasing conflict potential
reporting_angles: Interview residents about recent dog incidents; check if specific park or block is hotspot
Reach out to NYPD and Parks enforcement to understand if patrols have shifted or if complaints reflect real increase in violations

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints jumped to 17 this week compared to a 5.6-per-week average over 8 weeks—a 202% spike (z-score: 3.74)—suggesting either storm damage, disease, or deferred maintenance affecting neighborhood canopy.
evidence: 17 dead/dying tree complaints this week vs. 5.6 weekly baseline (202% increase, z-score: 3.74)
Community board has filed repeated budget requests for 'Forestry services, including street tree maintenance'—signals chronic Parks Department resource shortage
137 damaged tree complaints over past 90 days (second-tier volume issue), suggesting broader tree health stress
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks to document visible tree damage; photograph and geomap clusters
Interview Parks Department on maintenance backlog and response timeline; cross-check with budget request history showing repeated funding denials

themes_detail.label: Street/Sidewalk Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 18 last week from a baseline of 3.2 per week over 8 weeks—a 454% spike (z-score: 6.05)—indicating potential commercial or construction activity disrupting outdoor spaces.
evidence: 18 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 3.2 weekly baseline (454% spike, z-score: 6.05)
Companion spike: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 11 three weeks ago (319% increase, z-score: 3.23), suggesting sustained commercial/industrial activity
South Shore Industrial Center and 4450 Arthur Kill Road development applications filed and in review—potential construction or new facility noise sources
reporting_angles: Identify commercial or construction source of noise; verify against DOB permit data (737 total filings in district, including 282 new buildings)
Interview residents about timing and type of noise; cross-reference with active ULURP and non-ULURP applications to assess development-driven disruption

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Calls Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints surged to 18 last week versus a baseline of 6.1 per week over 8 weeks—a 194% increase (z-score: 6.25)—potentially indicating rising disorder, minor crime, or enforcement-adjacent incidents warranting investigation.
evidence: 18 non-emergency police complaints last week vs. 6.1 weekly baseline (194% spike, z-score: 6.25)
Community board has filed repeated budget requests for 'Provide a new NYPD facility'—signals perceived public safety resource gap
Spike is concurrent with unleashed dog complaints and street noise complaints, suggesting broader neighborhood disorder or enforcement visibility change
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD 120 Precinct to learn what types of non-emergency calls spiked; request incident data to categorize underlying issues
Interview residents about their safety perceptions and recent incidents; ask if complaints reflect new problems or increased reporting

themes_detail.label: Vacant Lot Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints jumped to 4 last week from a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1500% spike (z-score: 5.67)—pointing to sudden blight, dumping, or maintenance failure on one or more vacant properties.
evidence: 4 lot condition complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% spike, z-score: 5.67)
Community board repeatedly requests 'Increase enforcement of illegal dumping laws'—suggests chronic vacancy/dumping problem
Spike coincides with active development applications (South Shore Industrial Center, 4450 Arthur Kill Road) and ongoing street reconstruction projects
reporting_angles: Geomap the 4 lot condition complaints to identify specific properties; inspect for dumping, overgrowth, or structural hazards
Interview Sanitation Department on enforcement capacity and timeline for abatement; connect to repeated budget request history
